--- title: "Final syllable matching" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_FINAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_FINAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Emparejar sílaba final*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_FINAL.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Final syllable matching, from age 4 to 5 (4,315 administrations in 6 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .38. AUC .58–.66 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2014 526 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 5 (526) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child selects from an array of three pictures the one whose name ends with the same syllable as the object depicted above. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 28/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:-------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|-------------------:| | 526|Identificar sílabas |Estímulo y opciones en pantalla | 5| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 4, 4.2, 4.3, 5, 5.1| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **526.** 5 ítems; el ejemplo está en una actividad aparte (2014). *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![526 · Identificar sílabas](../../figuras/plataforma/526.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 526"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](../CF523.en.qmd) and [rapid naming](../RAN.en.qmd). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.2| 526| 2011| 131|2015/16 | 813| 0| 813| 33| | 4.2| 2014| 2012| 157|2016/17 | 390| 386| 0| 17| | 4.2| 526| 2012| 157|2016/17 | 389| 385| 0| 17| | 4.2| 526| 2013| 186|2017/18 | 566| 558| 8| 23| | 4.2| 526| 2014| 626|2018/19 | 388| 6| 382| 20| | 4.2| 526| 2015| 906|2019/20 | 428| 0| 428| 21| | 4.3| 526| 2014| 627|2018/19 | 385| 0| 385| 20| | 5.1| 526| 2010| 66|2015/16 | 956| 261| 693| 36| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----:|----------:|---:|----------------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 2014| 4.2| 386| 2012| 0.74| 0.44| 1| -1.12| 25.65| 0.00| | 526| 4.2| 949| 2012, 2013, 2014| 1.99| 1.17| 2| 0.12| 10.22| 0.00| | 526| 5.1| 261| 2010| 2.85| 1.42| 3| 0.09| 2.30| 18.01| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–5 correct responses. | Form| Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----:|----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 2014| 4.2| 386|0–1 |0–1 |0–5 | | | 526| 4.2| 949|0–4 |0–4 |0–5 | | | 526| 5.1| 261|0–5 |0–5 |0–5 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .38 (median .38, 1 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .46. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2014| 4.2| 4.3| 372| 0.35| 0.38| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .36–.55. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Oral morphosyntax (4.2, r = .33); Letter knowledge (4.3, r = .27); Verbal memory (5.1, r = .29). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .58–.66. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .58–.61. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_FINAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .55–.61 (2 time points; 249–431 children). ## Provisional norms | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----:|----------:|---:|----------------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2014| 4.2| 386| 2012| 0| 0| 0| 0| 1| 1| 1| | 526| 4.2| 949| 2012, 2013, 2014| 0| 0| 1| 1| 2| 3| 4| | 526| 4.3| 385| 2014| 1| 1| 1| 2| 3| 4| 4| | 526| 5.1| 261| 2010| 1| 1| 1| 2| 3| 4| 5| Each form (platform code) has its own norms, because the forms need not measure on the same scale. **Floor effect.** At 4.2 (form 2014) and 4.2 (form 526) P10 coincides with the worst possible score (at 4.2 (form 2014), P25 too): many children are tied at the minimum and the norms do not distinguish between them. At those time points this task cannot be used to grade difficulty. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_FINAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. If the same children took them, **linear equating** is also computed, which puts the second form on the scale of the first, together with the correlation between forms (parallel-forms reliability). If the groups differ, the difference mixes form and cohort. | Time point| Form 1| Form 2|Comparison | d (2 − 1)| SD ratio|Verdict | r between forms|Equating | |----------:|------:|------:|:-------------|---------:|--------:|:----------------|---------------:|:-----------------------| | 4.2| 2014| 526|same children | 1.23| 2.67|different scales | .26|2014 = 0.41 × 526 + 0.0 | ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.2| 2,627| 0.100| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.2| 2,893| -0.015| 0.695| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.2| 2,907| 0.109| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 4.2| 2,974| 0.178| | |School SES (ρ) | 4.3| 356| 0.074| 0.164| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.3| 341| 0.041| 0.707| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.3| 365| 0.081| 0.121| |School (ICC) | 4.3| 385| 0.145| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 956| 0.095| 0.003| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 872| -0.031| 0.652| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 871| 0.124| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 956| 0.225| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Final syllable matching” (codes 2014 and 526; LEEDUCA battery) assesses syllable awareness (final syllable identification). The examiner presents each item orally, supported by a picture on the screen, and records the child's oral response. It comprises 5 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 7 sessions, from 4 to 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .46 (N = 1,762, 5 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 4 months) was ρ = .38. Stability across time points was ρ = .38. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .58–.61. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 5.1 (form 526) (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Floor effect at 4.2 (form 2014) (more than 15% with zero correct). - Floor effect in the norms at 4.2 (form 2014) and 4.2 (form 526): at least 10% of children have the worst possible score, so P10 does not exist. At those time points the "severe" and "very severe" levels must not be assigned with this task (study M3). - The task has 2 forms; in 1 of 1 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
